title: Match Deep Dive: Pattern Destructuring
story: You've been matching on single values — but what if you need to check TWO things at once? Like a username AND a password? Or a coordinate pair? Match can destructure multiple values in one elegant expression.
why: Match can destructure tuples, nested Options, and combined patterns — checking multiple values at once collapses nested if-else chains into readable pattern tables.
analogy: Tuple matching is like checking multiple security cameras at once — instead of watching one screen, then another, you see all feeds on one wall and spot patterns instantly.
try_it: Write a function `classify_triangle(a: Int, b: Int, c: Int) -> Str`. Match on the tuple and return: 'Equilateral' if all equal, 'Isosceles' if any two equal, 'Scalene' if all different. Test with (3,3,3), (5,5,8), and (3,4,5).
tips: Parentheses group values into tuples for matching: `(val1, val2, val3)`
Pattern order matters — XIOM matches top to bottom, first matching arm wins
Use `_` as a wildcard when you don't care about a specific value in that position
common_mistakes: Writing `(Some(x), Ok(y))` when one side isn't wrapped — the tuple must match the exact types
Forgetting to handle all combinations — with 2 booleans there are 4 cases, with 2 Options there are 2
Putting a general pattern like `(x, y)` BEFORE more specific ones like `(0, 0)` — order matters!
